Description: The release version to download, e.g. 0.1.808 (see https://github.com/openOMSI-Project/openOMSI/releases for the latest). Change this and click Update to switch versions.

If set, the server files will not be automatically downloaded when the instance is updated. Turn this on if you upload the server files yourself (e.g. manually, or because this instance has no outbound internet access). Leave it off for the normal behaviour: Update downloads the selected version only if it isn't already installed.

This server has no window and draws nothing, but still needs a graphics backend to initialize. On a host with no GPU (e.g. a bare-metal server), pick a Mesa software renderer: Vulkan (lavapipe) is the default and usually fastest; OpenGL (llvmpipe) is a fallback if Vulkan initialization fails. Both are installed automatically. If you have a real GPU available to the container, you generally do not need to change this.

Path to the original OMSI 2 installation that this server will use for its map, vehicle and mod content (the folder containing Omsi.exe, maps and Vehicles). Relative to this instance's working directory, e.g. ./omsi2 if you uploaded the installation into a folder named omsi2 here; an absolute path also works.
Shown in the launcher's server list and to players when they join.
Message of the day shown to joining players.
Path to the map's global.cfg, relative to the OMSI 2 folder, e.g. maps/Berlin-Spandau/global.cfg.

Buses players may drive, separated by ; (e.g. Vehicles/MAN_SD200/MAN_SD77.bus). Leave blank to allow every bus installed on the server. The players' vehicle menu offers only these, and a player driving another bus is sent away.
The world date the session starts at.
The world clock time the session starts at.
How fast the world clock runs: 1 = real time, 2 = twice as fast, up to 30. Ignored when 'Follow real time' is on.
The world clock follows this machine's real date and time. Date/Time above then only set the very first moment, and Clock speed and an admin's clock command are ignored.

IANA time zone the server's clock uses (e.g. Europe/Prague, Europe/Berlin, UTC). Matters mainly with 'Follow real time' on: the container usually runs in UTC by default, so the in-game clock can otherwise be hours off from your own.
A weather file (e.g. Weather/#CAVOK.owt) or 'auto' to cycle weather automatically.
The weather follows the real METAR report of an airport, refreshed every ten minutes. Weather above then only sets the first moment, and admins cannot change it.
Airport ICAO code to sync weather from, e.g. EDDB. Leave blank to use the one nearest the map. Only used when 'Sync weather to real METAR' is on.
How much AI traffic the world simulates.
Enables simulated timetable buses.
Enables simulated passengers at stops and aboard buses.

Factor on the map's own passenger demand for the time of day: 1 = as the map says, 0.5 = half, 2 = twice (0 to 3). 0 stops new people appearing but keeps existing passengers on (to switch passengers off entirely, use Passengers above). Can be changed by admins while the server runs; players already aboard are unaffected.
The UDP port players connect to directly.
HTTP/WebSocket port used for browser-based players, /status, /icon.png, /admin and /players.
Maximum number of concurrent players.
Starts a free cloudflared quick tunnel so players can join over WebSocket without port forwarding.
Tile streaming radius around each player's bus, in metres. 0 loads the whole map.
Enables GET /players (live map data: position, heading, speed). Off by default for privacy.

Players who enter this password with /admin get full Administration menu access: send players away, bring them, the clock, its speed, the weather, the traffic and the passengers. Also required for the web admin panel and its POST /admin API (clock, weather, say, kick). At least 12 characters. Leave blank to disable admin access.

Players who enter this password with /admin get moderator powers: see players, send them away, and talk to them - but not the clock, weather, traffic, passengers, or bringing players to their bus. At least 12 characters. Leave blank to disable moderators.

Who may reach the web admin panel (http://127.0.0.1:<web_port>/admin/) and its API. Local: this machine only (not through the tunnel or a proxy). Remote: also over HTTPS through the proxies listed in Trusted proxies below (this machine by default - with the Cloudflare tunnel on, that is the public tunnel, so the passwords alone guard it then). Off: nobody.
Other https:// sites whose pages may use the admin web panel's API, separated by ;. Leave blank unless you are embedding the panel in a website of your own.

Addresses of reverse proxies allowed to forward admin web panel traffic when Admin web panel access is set to Remote. Leave blank if you are not running your own reverse proxy in front of this server.
The header a trusted admin proxy uses to name the real client: x-forwarded-for (its last address - Caddy, nginx, Cloudflare), x-real-ip, or cf-connecting-ip. Only this header is believed.
The header used to identify players who connect by WebSocket through a proxy on this machine: x-forwarded-for, or cf-connecting-ip with Cloudflare's proxy (the orange cloud) in front.
GreenTeaSpeak channel id or name that players are moved into for proximity voice chat. Leave blank to disable voice chat.
Sent to every joining player so their game can enter the voice channel. Keeps strangers on the voice server out.
The unique id of the GreenTeaSpeak voice server (shown in GreenTeaSpeak's server info panel). Required for voice chat to work.
Maximum distance players can hear each other, muffled through bus bodywork.
Gives drivers a bindable map-wide bus radio on top of proximity voice chat (default key: X). Only used when voice chat is configured.

A player whose bus this server does not have sends it the files that bus uses (the variant and paint driven, not the whole pack); the server keeps them and passes them on to other players, so nobody sees a stand-in. Taken without asking and kept after a restart. With this on and Allowed vehicles above left blank, players may choose any bus.
Days an uploaded bus is kept when nobody drives it. When disk space runs short, buses nobody drives now go first, the least recently used first - no bus is refused purely for its size.

A player who joins without the server's map gets it from the server (the map and the objects, splines and vehicles it uses - can be gigabytes for a big map). Off: players install the map themselves and are told which one is missing, keeping the server's bandwidth free for players' buses.
